title: Full 18S Metabarcoding of Environmental Samples with Nanopore Sequencing
author: Quentin Blandenier
materials: Qubit High Sensitivity Double Strand (HS dsDNA)

As soon as your sample is collected it will be impacted by your storage condition, which matters a lot for microbial organisms, in particular, as they have a fast turnover. Consequently, you should avoid as much as possible to delay the return to the laboratory. In the meantime, you can use a cooler with ice or at least avoid storing your sample in a hot vehicle. Alternatively, aliquot ~ 2-2.5 mL of nucleotide buffer, such as LifeGuard Soil Preservation Solution (Qiagen) , in 5 ml tubes before starting the sampling, and place ~ 1 g of soil to stabilize it until the return to the lab.

From now on, follow the protocol DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit from Qiagen (corresponding here to steps 13-26). First centrifuge the PowerBead Pro Tube at 15,000 x g for 00:01:00 . Qiagen_DNeasyPowerSoilProKit.pdf

Despite being optimized for soil samples, the DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit (Qiagen) can also be used for liquid samples, such as water, in order to limit DNA extraction bias when comparing different types of samples. Thaw the AMPure XP Beads (AXP), the EDTA and the Native Barcodes (NB01-96) at room temperature. Keep the beads at room temperature at all times, but place the two others on ice. Vortex the EDTA and spin it down. The Native barcodes plate and the NEB Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix have to be spun down and then mixed by performing several pipette mixes.

In a new 96-well plate or 8-stripes tubes, add the reagents in the following order per well: Nuclease-free water 3 µL , End-prepped DNA 0.75 µL , Native Barcode (NB01-96) 1.25 µL and Blunt/TA Ligase Master Mix 5 µL for a total of 10 µL . Always pipette mix 10 - 20 times between each addition. Select a unique barcode for every sample to be run together on the same flow cell. Up to 96 samples can be barcoded and combined in one experiment. We used a multi-channel pipette to distribute the Nuclease-free water, the End-prepped DNA and the Native Barcode, but used a single-channel pipette for the Blunt/TA Ligase to avoid any loss of this enzyme.

steps.title: Collect environmental sample
steps.instruction: Select a pristine, undisturbed site and collect ~0.5‑1 kg soil, ~50‑200 g dry leaves or bark, or ~1‑2 L water into a clean plastic bag or bottle; record date, location, coordinates, material type, sampler name, take photos, avoid stones, roots, animals, wear gloves and sterilize tools with ethanol or bleach.

steps.title: Store samples before extraction
steps.instruction: Store soils at –20 °C for a few days (‑80 °C for long‑term); store water samples in the fridge overnight (do not freeze water samples).

steps.title: Prepare laminar flow cabinet
steps.instruction: Clean cabinet with ethanol, place a microscale, DNeasy PowerSoil Pro kit (closed), 2 mL tube rack, gloves, 5 mL tubes, cleaning paper, Bunsen burner, lighter, pen and benchtop centrifuge; keep all reagents closed and sterilize with ethanol before use.

steps.title: Process water samples (pre‑filter)
steps.instruction: Sterilize a 250 µm mesh filter (e.g., SE filter GP2‑1100) with bleach; filter water through the mesh to remove large particles before downstream steps.

steps.title: Process leaf or bark samples
steps.instruction: Weigh ~5 g leaf or bark into a clean bottle, add 250 mL sterile water (e.g., Deer Park), shake vigorously for 1 min, then filter through a 250 µm mesh to remove large particles.

steps.title: Filter water onto 0.2 µm membrane
steps.instruction: Pour filtered water (or filtrate from leaf/bark) onto a 0.2 µm Nalgene cellulose nitrate membrane (50 mm, catalog 121‑0020) until the membrane saturates; use a vacuum pump if desired and work over a Bunsen burner to avoid airborne contamination.

steps.title: Transfer membrane to PowerBead tube
steps.instruction: In the laminar hood, cut the saturated membrane into two pieces with a sterilized scalpel, place both pieces into a labeled PowerBead Pro tube; sterilize scalpel with ethanol between samples; optionally store filters frozen overnight before proceeding.

steps.title: Thaw and weigh soil samples
steps.instruction: Remove soil tubes from fridge or freezer, let thaw; weigh ~0.25 g soil into a clean 5 mL tube using a metallic spoon, avoiding mineral particles, roots, animals; transfer to a labeled PowerBead Pro tube; sterilize spoon with ethanol and Bunsen burner before each use.

steps.title: Bead‑beating lysate
steps.instruction: Place PowerBead Pro tubes in FastPrep‑24 homogenizer (MP Biomedicals) and run 2 cycles: 20 s at 4 m/s followed by 5 min break; label tubes on top and side before running.

steps.title: PowerSoil Pro kit – CD2 step
steps.instruction: Transfer the lysate supernatant (~500‑600 µL) to a clean 2 mL microcentrifuge tube; add 200 µL Solution CD2, vortex 5 s; centrifuge 15 000 ×g for 1 min; avoid pellet and transfer up to 700 µL supernatant to a new 2 mL tube.

steps.title: PowerSoil Pro kit – CD3 step
steps.instruction: Add 600 µL Solution CD3 to the tube, vortex 5 s.

steps.title: Load lysate onto MB spin column
steps.instruction: Load 650 µL of the lysate onto an MB Spin Column, centrifuge 15 000 ×g for 1 min; discard flow‑through; repeat loading until all lysate has passed through the column.

steps.title: Wash column with EA solution
steps.instruction: Place the MB Spin Column into a clean 2 mL collection tube; add 500 µL Solution EA, centrifuge 15 000 ×g for 1 min; discard flow‑through; return column to the same collection tube.

steps.title: Wash column with C5 solution
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL Solution C5 to the column, centrifuge 15 000 ×g for 1 min; discard flow‑through; place column into a new 2 mL collection tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA from column
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at up to 16 000 ×g for 2 min; transfer the MB Spin Column into a new 1.5 mL Elution Tube; add 50‑100 µL Solution C6 (used 100 µL) to the center of the white membrane; incubate as per kit instructions and collect eluate.

steps.title: Quantify DNA with Qubit
steps.instruction: Take 2 µL of each eluate and measure concentration using the Qubit High Sensitivity dsDNA kit; observed range 4.6‑114 ng/µL (mean 46.5 ng/µL).

steps.title: Aliquot DNA for bench work
steps.instruction: Aliquot 20 µL of each DNA extract into a tube for bench‑side work, keep the remaining 80 µL as sterile stock; label tubes with project, sample name, date, extractor, and “Aliquot” or “Stock”; store stocks at –20 °C.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality with Nanodrop
steps.instruction: Measure 1 µL of each DNA extract on a Nanodrop; concentrations ranged 6.3‑184 ng/µL (mean 62.5 ng/µL); 260/280 ratios 1.91‑2.48 (mean 1.93); 260/230 ratios 0.01‑0.75 (mean 0.65).

steps.title: Check DNA integrity on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Run 3 µL of each DNA sample on a 1 % TA agarose gel at 70 V for 3 h with a 1 kb+ ladder (Biolabs) to evaluate fragment size (expected 4‑5 kb, observed 5‑8 kb).

steps.title: Dilute DNA to target concentration
steps.instruction: Dilute each DNA sample to 10 ng/µL (or to 5 ng/µL if initial concentration is low) by adding elution buffer; e.g., mix 6 µL DNA with appropriate volume of buffer.

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: For each 24 µL reaction combine: 12.5 µL 2× GoTaq Master Mix, 0.5 µL 10 µM primer S1, 10.5 µL 10 µM primer RibB, add nuclease‑free water to 24 µL. Multiply the volume by (number of samples + 1 extraction blank + 1 PCR negative control + extra).

steps.title: Primer information
steps.instruction: Dilute primers to 10 µM. Forward S1: 5′‑AACCTGGTTGATCCTGCC‑3′. Reverse RibB: 5′‑GATCCTTCTGCAGGTTCA CC‑3′ (from Fiore‑Donno et al. 2005/2008).

steps.title: Set up PCR reactions
steps.instruction: Dispense 24 µL of master mix into each tube or well; add 1 µL of 10 ng/µL DNA (or appropriate volume to reach 10 ng) to reach 25 µL total; mix gently.

steps.title: Run PCR in triplicate
steps.instruction: Thermal cycler program: 95 °C 2 min (1 cycle); 33 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 48 °C 30 s, 72 °C 4 min; final extension 72 °C 5 min; hold 10 °C. Perform three independent replicates per sample.

steps.title: Verify PCR products
steps.instruction: Run 3 µL of each PCR product on a 1 % TBE or TA gel at 100 V for 1 h with a 1 kb+ ladder to confirm correct band size.

steps.title: Pool triplicate PCRs per sample
steps.instruction: After confirming good bands, combine the three replicates of each sample in a 0.2 mL tube (one tube per sample); perform a quick spin to collect liquid.

steps.title: Magnetic bead clean‑up (Mag‑Bind)
steps.instruction: Remove Mag‑Bind Total Pure NGS beads from the fridge 30 min before use; add beads at a 1:1 volume ratio to each pooled PCR (e.g., 30 µL beads to 30 µL PCR); vortex beads 10 s before adding; incubate 10 min at RT on a Hula mixer at 160 rpm; magnet 2 min; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Ethanol washes
steps.instruction: With tubes still on the magnet, add 200 µL freshly prepared 70 % ethanol, wait 30 s, remove supernatant; repeat for a second wash; then dry beads for ~30 s (do not over‑dry).

steps.title: Elute purified PCR product
steps.instruction: Add 31 µL Elution Buffer (15 µL for the PCR negative control); incubate 10 min at 37 °C on Hula mixer 160 rpm; magnet 2 min; remove 30 µL eluate (retain 30 µL).

steps.title: Quantify purified DNA
steps.instruction: Measure each purified sample, mock community, and two negative controls with Qubit HS dsDNA; concentrations ranged 45‑116 ng/µL (controls undetectable).

steps.title: Calculate library input amount
steps.instruction: For 2 kb fragments, 200 fmol ≈ 260 ng total DNA. Required input volume is 11.5 µL, so target concentration ≈ 22.6 ng/µL (acceptable 20‑25 ng/µL). Dilute each sample to ~22.6 ng/µL, aiming for a final volume of 15‑30 µL.

steps.title: Concentrate overly dilute samples
steps.instruction: If a sample cannot reach ~22 ng/µL, use a speed‑vacuum concentrator to reduce volume before final dilution.

steps.title: Prepare DNA Control Sample (DCS)
steps.instruction: Thaw DCS at room temperature, vortex, keep on ice; prepare NEBNext Ultra II End‑Repair/dA‑tailing reagents on ice; do not vortex the enzyme mix, vortex the buffer.

steps.title: Dilute DCS
steps.instruction: Add 105 µL Elution Buffer directly to the DCS tube, mix gently by pipetting, spin down.

steps.title: End‑prep mix per sample
steps.instruction: Combine 1 µL diluted DCS, 1.75 µL Ultra II End‑prep Reaction Buffer, 0.75 µL Ultra II End‑prep Enzyme Mix (total 3.5 µL). For library negative control replace DCS with 1 µL Elution Buffer.

steps.title: Add end‑prep mix to samples
steps.instruction: Dispense 3.5 µL end‑prep mix into each well of a 96‑well plate or 8‑strip tubes using a single‑channel pipette.

steps.title: Add amplicon DNA to end‑prep
steps.instruction: Add 11.5 µL of the 200 fmol amplicon DNA to each well (total volume 15 µL); mix by pipetting (use multi‑channel for speed).

steps.title: End‑prep incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate 20 °C for 5 min then 65 °C for 5 min in a thermal cycler; quick spin; the reaction can be stored overnight if needed.

steps.title: Stop ligation with EDTA
steps.instruction: Add 1 µL EDTA to each well to stop ligation, mix thoroughly, quick spin.

steps.title: Pool barcoded libraries
steps.instruction: Combine all barcoded samples into a single 1.5 mL LoBind tube.

steps.title: AMPure XP bead clean‑up (0.4×)
steps.instruction: Vortex AMPure XP beads for 30 s, add 0.44 µL beads per sample (≈0.4× ratio), mix well, incubate 10 min at RT on Hula mixer; prepare 80 % ethanol fresh.

steps.title: Bead capture and washes
steps.instruction: Place tube on magnetic rack 5 min, discard supernatant; wash beads twice with 700 µL 80 % ethanol, removing ethanol each time; dry beads ~30 s (do not over‑dry).

steps.title: Elute library from beads
steps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 35 µL nuclease‑free water, incubate 10 min at 37 °C with gentle flicking every 2 min for 10 s; magnet 1 min, retain 35 µL eluate in a clean LoBind tube; store at 4 °C (do not freeze).

steps.title: Quantify final library
steps.instruction: Measure 1 µL of the eluted library with Qubit HS dsDNA; optionally check with Nanodrop.

steps.title: Dilute library for loading
steps.instruction: Target 10‑20 fmol in 12 µL (≈1.1‑2.17 ng/µL for 2 kb fragments). Prepare a larger volume (≈30 µL) by calculating DNA volume = (desired concentration × final volume)/measured concentration and adding Elution Buffer to reach final volume; verify concentration with 2‑3 Qubit measurements and Nanodrop if needed; keep library on ice, leftover can be stored at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare flow cell reagents
steps.instruction: Thaw Sequencing Buffer (SB), Library Beads (LIB), Flow Cell Tether (FCT), and Flow Cell Flush (FCF) at room temperature; vortex and spin down each.

steps.title: Make priming mix
steps.instruction: In a clean 1.7 mL tube combine 1170 µL Flow Cell Flush (FCF) with 30 µL Flow Cell Tether (FCT); invert to mix; keep mix at room temperature before loading.

steps.title: Prime flow cell (first step)
steps.instruction: Open MinION lid, place flow cell under the clip, perform flow‑cell check; load 200 µL priming mix into the priming port (not SpotON); draw back 10‑30 µL with a P1000 set to 200 µL to remove bubbles; verify continuous buffer across sensor array.

steps.title: Prime flow cell (second step)
steps.instruction: Load an additional 800 µL priming mix into the priming port; wait 5 min.

steps.title: Load library onto flow cell
steps.instruction: Mix the prepared library gently by pipetting up‑and‑down; load 75 µL of library into the SpotON sample port dropwise, ensuring each drop enters before adding the next; avoid loading into the priming port.

steps.title: Start sequencing run
steps.instruction: Run with settings: kit SQK‑NBD114.96, 400 bps, 100 h, minimum read length 200 bp, fast basecalling, barcoding on.

steps.title: Monitor and finish run
steps.instruction: Pore activity is high initially, declines after ~1 day; authors recommend running up to ~72 h without pause; optional flow‑cell wash per ONT protocol after run.

steps.title: Download run report
steps.instruction: Retrieve sequencing run report; optionally wash and reuse flow cell according to ONT instructions.
